panels.title: Resources: each Cloud Run service's CPU, memory, instances, concurrency and start-up (open a row)
No disk on a Cloud Run service

options.content: **Cloud Run services have no disk.** A file a container writes is held in its memory, so a service's "disk space" is its **Memory** chart: files that grow show as memory climbing to the red line, then as a container killed for memory. Real disk is on the databases (each one's disk space is on its area's page and on Databases) and in the buckets. A **red line** is the line the pager uses (tpa-platform's alert policies); a **grey line** is a limit the service is set to.

panels.title: auth-db: backups and point-in-time recovery (seven days of logs)
Backups in the last 30 hours
panels.description: auth-db's successful automated backups in the last 30 hours (`sql_automated_backups`, windowStatus STATUS_SUCCEEDED) and its failed ones (`sql_backup_failures`). The alert, `auth-db-backup-missing` (urgent), judges today's backup, from 14:00 UTC: the window from 09:00 UTC closed an hour before with no successful backup while the instance was up all day. This tile shows a successful backup in the last 30 hours, so a missed night turns it red about two hours after the page (30 hours after the night before's backup). One backup a night, starting in a four-hour window from 09:00 UTC: two have landed up to 26.1 hours apart, so a healthy instance always has one in 30 hours. ✕ none in 30 h, red: none while auth-db reported for 29 of the 30 hours or more; an instance started since reads "no backup yet". ✕ a backup failed, red: its newest failure (`auth-db-backup-failed`) is later than its newest success, each by the hour, so a failed attempt that a later attempt made good reads ✓ backed up, and a night that failed reads ✕ at once. The failed count, red from one, counts every failed entry in the 30 hours: one bad night writes several failed attempts and a final failure, so it is entries, not nights. ✓ backed up. Point-in-time recovery replays its seven days of logs from a backup taken before the minute chosen. "database stopped": stopped on purpose (its activation policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing. Reads "paused" or "database stopped", in no colour, while `auth-db` is stopped on purpose (the service's TPA_PAUSED_JOBS, TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES).

defaults.noValue: @@R,auth-db,@@not reporting@@

Point-in-time recovery keeps seven days of logs. "database stopped": stopped on purpose (its activation policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing. Reads "paused" or "database stopped", in no colour, while `auth-db` is stopped on purpose (the service's TPA_PAUSED_JOBS, TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES).

panels.title: Event publisher heartbeat (batches completed)
panels.description: One `publisher_alive` line a minute while auth's event publisher completes its batches, none while it does not (`auth_events_publisher_alive`): none for five minutes opens `auth-events-lag`, for fifteen `auth-events-stalled` (urgent; first sign-ins refused).

defaults.noValue: Missing: no publisher_alive line in this range, so publishing has stopped or auth-event-publisher is not reporting

panels.title: Event publisher instances
panels.description: auth-event-publisher's instances. With none, no sign-in event reaches records: a first sign-in waits (`mirror_stale`), and `auth-events-lag` opens.

defaults.noValue: No instance reported: auth-event-publisher is kept warm, so it is down or not reporting

panels.title: Sign-in protection, staff laptops and one-time passes
Sign-ins paused after wrong attempts
panels.description: One per account whose sign-in auth paused after wrong attempts, by the pause (`code`: account, factor, factor_ceiling, factor_repeated) and whose account (`class`: staff or outside), from auth's messenger (`auth_sign_in_protection`; `auth-sign-in-repeated`, `auth-sign-in-ceiling`, `auth-sign-in-code-surge` and the staff policies read it). Never the account, an address or a code.

defaults.noValue: None in this range

panels.title: Breached-password lookups with no answer
panels.description: A breached-password lookup that gave auth no answer, so a sign-in or a password set was refused (`auth_breach_corpus_unavailable`; `auth-breach-corpus-unavailable`), by when (`code`: set or login) and why (`class`: timeout or read).

defaults.noValue: None in this range

panels.title: Texted codes refused at a day's ceiling
panels.description: Members' texted codes auth refused because the estate's day is spent, by where (`code`: offer or send) and which ceiling (`class`: soft, past the setting; hard, past twice it) (`auth_sms_codes_estate_ceiling`; `auth-texted-codes-ceiling`), and applicants' set-up codes refused at theirs (`auth_sms_codes_registration_ceiling`; `auth-registration-codes-ceiling`).

defaults.noValue: None in this range

panels.title: Staff laptops: waiting, approved, mismatched, copied
panels.description: auth's staff laptop lines (`auth_staff_devices`), from auth and its jobs: a laptop waiting for approval (`device_pending`), one approved (`device_approved`, `outcome` operator or admin), an approval or binding auth did not write (`device_tag_mismatch`) and a copied device cookie a second browser used (`device_cookie_superseded`); `auth-device-*` read them. Never the person or the laptop.

defaults.noValue: No staff laptop event in this range

panels.title: Device-bound staff sessions
panels.description: auth's device-bound staff sessions (`auth_bound_sessions`): bound, refreshed, a binding Chrome declined, a refused proof (at `register` or `refresh`), a session ended after five wrong proofs (`binding_guessed`; `auth-binding-guessed`) and a binding auth did not write. Never the person or the session.

defaults.noValue: No bound-session event in this range

panels.title: One-time sign-in passes issued and used
panels.description: A one-time sign-in a TPA administrator issued for a member of staff, or that member of staff signed in with (`auth_sign_in_passes`; `auth-sign-in-pass-issued`, `auth-sign-in-pass-used`). Who, for whom and why are in auth's audit chain.

defaults.noValue: No sign-in pass issued or used in this range

panels.title: Executions, by job and result
panels.description: Completed executions of auth's jobs per interval. Two failed in a row open `jobs-failed` (R380); one opens the urgent `audit-chain` for the audit jobs.

defaults.noValue: No runs in this range

panels.title: Schedules that could not start their job
panels.description: Cloud Scheduler attempts for auth's schedules that finished in error, by schedule and status.

defaults.noValue: None in this range
